titleEn: For millennia, Aboriginal astronomers have explained the movement of stars, planets, eclipses and tides
titleZh: 数千年来，原住民天文学者如何解释星体运动、日月食与潮汐
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Australian Aboriginal people have seen the sky as an integral part of their world for at least 65,000 years. The Aboriginal sky is a world that reflects our Earth-bound world, so understanding the sky is an important part of understanding our place here on Earth.
paragraphs.zh: 澳大利亚原住民将天空视为他们世界不可分割的一部分至少有65，000年的历史。原住民的天空是一个反映我们地球世界的世界，因此了解天空是了解我们在地球上的重要组成部分。

paragraphs.en: As a result, Aboriginal songs, stories and art show evidence of thousands of years of studying and understanding the sky. And in the ancient Aboriginal traditions, we see the traces of giant intellectual achievements.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，土著人的歌曲、故事和艺术展示了数千年来研究和理解天空的证据。在古老的土著传统中，我们看到了巨大的智力成就的痕迹。

paragraphs.en: The stars and the planets
paragraphs.zh: 恒星和行星

paragraphs.en: In the clear black skies that predated streetlights and satellites, Aboriginal elders would look up at the sky night after night. They would see how all the stars rotate around us as if embedded in a crystal sphere, each night giving us a slightly different view.
paragraphs.zh: 在街灯和卫星出现之前，在清澈的夜空中，原住民的老人们会一夜又一夜地仰望天空，他们会看到所有的星星都围绕着我们旋转，就像嵌在一个水晶球里一样，每个晚上都给我们一个稍微不同的视角。

paragraphs.en: And they realised that not all stars are the same. While Western astronomers preached that the stars were constant in brightness, Aboriginal astronomers noticed that some, such as the famous Betelgeuse in Orion’s shoulder (in Western tradition) or at the front of his canoe (in Yolngu tradition, in Arnhem Land) brighten and dim over time.
paragraphs.zh: 他们意识到并非所有的恒星都是一样的。当西方天文学家宣扬恒星的亮度是恒定的时，土著天文学家注意到有些恒星，如猎户座肩膀上著名的参宿四（西方传统）或他独木舟前部的参宿四（阿纳姆地的Yolngu传统），会随着时间的推移而变亮或变暗。

paragraphs.en: Against that backdrop, Aboriginal astronomers saw the planets moving amongst the stars. They saw how most planets appear to move steadily along a path that modern astronomers call the ecliptic, and Wardaman people from the Northern Territory called “Yondorrin”. They understood how Mars would sometimes pause its steady travel across the sky, and backtrack a few steps, before resuming its forward march.
paragraphs.zh: 在这样的背景下，土著天文学家看到行星在恒星之间移动。他们看到大多数行星似乎是如何沿着一条被现代天文学家称为黄道的路径稳步沿着移动，来自北领地的沃达曼人称之为“Yondorrin”。他们理解火星有时会暂停其在天空中的稳定旅行，并后退几步，然后继续前进。

paragraphs.en: They understood how Venus, as the Morning Star, always rose just before dawn, or as the Evening Star set just after sunset, but never appeared high in the night sky..
paragraphs.zh: 他们明白金星作为晨星星星，总是在黎明前升起，或者作为昏星星星在日落后落下，但从来没有出现在夜空的高处。

paragraphs.en: Modern astronomers explain these movements in terms of planetary orbits. But the ancient Aboriginal astronomers fitted them into their own cultural framework, with stories of creator spirits, their stories always staying true to their careful observational data.
paragraphs.zh: 现代天文学家用行星轨道来解释这些运动，但古代土著天文学家将其纳入自己的文化框架，用造物主精神的故事来解释，他们的故事总是忠于他们仔细的观察数据。

paragraphs.en: Lunar and solar eclipses
paragraphs.zh: 月食和日食

paragraphs.en: A solar eclipse, that rare spine-chilling apparition when the Sun goes dark during the daytime, is caused by the Moon passing in front of the Sun.
paragraphs.zh: 日食是一种罕见的令人毛骨悚然的现象，当太阳在白天变暗时，它是由月亮从太阳前面经过引起的。

paragraphs.en: Some Aboriginal groups had figured this out too, and explained it as the Moon-man covering the Sun-woman as they made love. The Aboriginal astronomers passed this knowledge on across the generations, even though only about one in ten generations would actually witness a solar eclipse.
paragraphs.zh: 一些原住民团体也发现了这一点，并解释为月球人在做爱时覆盖太阳女人。原住民天文学家将这一知识代代相传，尽管只有大约十分之一的人会真正目睹日食。

paragraphs.en: On the other hand, a lunar eclipse, when the Moon goes blood red at night, is caused by Earth blocking the sunlight that normally lights up the Moon. This happens when the Sun and Moon are on exactly opposite sides of the sky, which is not at all obvious to the untrained eye.
paragraphs.zh: 另一方面，月食，当月亮在晚上变成血红色时，是由于地球阻挡了通常照亮月球的阳光造成的。这种情况发生在太阳和月亮正好在天空的相对两侧，这对未经训练的眼睛来说根本不明显。

paragraphs.en: What Aboriginal genius had that flash of insight, while watching a lunar eclipse, that this eclipse was caused by the precise juxtaposition of the Sun and Moon on opposite sides of the sky? That realisation was an important intellectual leap, and we won’t ever know the name of the ancient astronomer who first realised it.
paragraphs.zh: 什么样的土著天才在观看月食时突然领悟到，这种月食是由太阳和月亮在天空相对两侧的精确并列造成的？这一认识是一个重要的智力飞跃，我们永远不会知道第一个意识到这一点的古代天文学家的名字。

paragraphs.en: But we still see traces in the Aboriginal cultural legacy.
paragraphs.zh: 但我们仍然看到土著文化遗产的痕迹。

paragraphs.en: The movement of the tides
paragraphs.zh: 潮汐的运动

paragraphs.en: We are all familiar with the rise and fall of the tides on the beach. But their cause eluded astronomers for years.
paragraphs.zh: 我们都熟悉海滩上潮汐的涨落，但多年来天文学家们一直搞不清楚其原因。

paragraphs.en: Galileo failed to explain them, coming up with an entirely incorrect explanation which denied the Moon any role. In contrast, ancient Yolngu astronomers recognised the tides were caused by the Moon, and realised that you can predict the height of the tide from the phase of the Moon.
paragraphs.zh: 伽利略未能解释它们，提出了一个完全不正确的解释，否认月球的任何作用。相反，古代Yolngu天文学家认识到潮汐是由月球引起的，并意识到你可以预测潮汐的高度从月相。

paragraphs.en: Unfortunately we have no way of dating this knowledge. But given that other Aboriginal astronomical traditions stretch back many hundreds or thousands of years, it is likely that this Yolngu knowledge is far older than our modern Western understanding.
paragraphs.zh: 不幸的是，我们无法确定这些知识的年代，但考虑到其他土著人的天文传统可以追溯到数百年或数千年前，Yolngu的知识很可能比我们现代西方的理解要古老得多。

paragraphs.en: This enabled Yolngu people to safely navigate the crocodile-infested waters of the Arafura Sea, where Galileo surely would have perished.
paragraphs.zh: 这使得Yolngu人能够安全地在阿拉弗拉海的鳄鱼出没的沃茨航行，伽利略肯定会在那里丧生。

paragraphs.en: So this understanding of the sky went beyond simply understanding how the sky worked. It also had practical applications, enabling ancient Aboriginal people to navigate across and around Australia, and build sophisticated calendars which would help them manage the land and their food supply.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，这种对天空的理解不仅仅是理解天空是如何运作的，它还有实际的应用，使古代土著人能够在澳大利亚各地航行，并建立复杂的日历，帮助他们管理土地和食物供应。

paragraphs.en: Bringing different knowledges together
paragraphs.zh: 将不同的知识融合在一起

paragraphs.en: This ancient astronomical knowledge fits into the growing appreciation of the vast body of Aboriginal achievements in navigation, medicine and agriculture. By comparing modern science with Aboriginal culture, we can clearly see the depth and intellectual power of ancient Aboriginal cultures.
paragraphs.zh: 这些古老的天文知识，与原住民在航海、医学、农业等方面的巨大成就，正日益受到人们的重视。将现代科学与原住民文化相比较，我们可以清楚地看到古代原住民文化的深度和智慧力量。

paragraphs.en: This article itself, as well as our other work, is the result of bringing different knowledges together. One of us (Ray) has spent a lifetime studying the sky through astrophysics. The other (Bruce) observes the sky through Aboriginal eyes, and has learnt from traditional stories and paintings passed on by other Aboriginal people.
paragraphs.zh: 这篇文章本身，以及我们的其他作品，是不同知识融合的结果。我们中的一个（雷）花了一生的时间通过天体物理学研究天空;另一个（布鲁斯）通过土著人的眼睛观察天空，并从其他土著人流传的传统故事和绘画中学习。

paragraphs.en: When science meets Aboriginal culture, we enrich our understanding of both.
paragraphs.zh: 当科学与原住民文化相遇时，我们丰富了对两者的理解。
